vlm_3p_explanation: This spectrum represents a mixed chloride-bearing sodium orthophosphate ('3-P') grain. It exhibits a strong salt backbone at 23 u and 63 u (prom=0.418) and passes the orthophosphate triplet criteria: the 125 u Na+(NaPO3) peak (prom=0.118) is clearly aligned with the 125 u green band rather than the 129 u carbonate band (diff_125_minus_129=+0.0552), alongside positive features in the 165 u Na+(Na2HPO4) band (prom=0.047 >= 0.045) and the 187 u Na+(Na3PO4) band (prom=0.068 >= 0.065), while the 81 u chloride peak remains below the pure 3-Cl veto thresholds (p81=0.292 <= 0.30, 81u/63u ratio=0.90, p139=0.107 < 0.145).

Textbook sodium orthophosphate (3-P) spectrum displaying a strong salt backbone at 23 u and 63 u (prom=0.322) and a well-resolved orthophosphate triplet at 125 u (prom=0.143, apex at 126.5 u with diff_125_minus_129=+0.0182 favoring 125 u over 129 u carbonate), 165 u (prom=0.186, apex at 166.5 u), and 187 u (prom=0.256, apex at 189.5 u), with negligible chloride interference (81 u prom=0.028, 139 u prom=0.008).

The spectrum fails the orthophosphate triplet criteria. In the 120-135 u region, there is no distinct 125 u Na+(NaPO3) peak; instead, the weak feature aligns with the 129 u carbonate band (apex at 131.0 u, prom 125 u = 0.079 vs 129 u = 0.088, diff_125_minus_129 = -0.0086). Furthermore, despite noisy baseline fluctuations yielding nominal telemetry prominences at 165 u (0.071) and 187 u (0.089, apex at 184.0 u), the zoomed anion window shows no distinct peaks at 165 u or 187 u, and instead exhibits strong 81 u (prom = 0.248), 103 u, and 143 u hydroxide/chloride features.

This spectrum is clearly non-3-P. It lacks a strong Na+(NaOH) 63u salt backbone (h=0.43, prom=0.082), shows a strong 39u peak (or shifted hydronium/water cluster with 23u anchor at 0.65 us), and in the zoomed anion window (70-195 u) exhibits only high-frequency baseline noise rather than distinct orthophosphate triplet peaks. Furthermore, the 125u vs 129u check fails (p125=0.063 vs p129=0.088, diff_125_minus_129=-0.0258 with apex at 129.5u), and the apparent prominences at 165u (0.104) and 187u (0.093) are purely noise spikes.

This spectrum is a classic carbonate ('3-Car') look-alike rather than a true '3-P' grain. The primary anion feature in the 120-135 u region peaks sharply at 129.5 u inside the red 129 u carbonate band (prom=0.456 vs 125 u prom=0.323, diff_125_minus_129=-0.1514), accompanied by a characteristic carbonate feature near 85 u. Furthermore, the zoomed plot confirms the absence of real orthophosphate peaks at 165 u (just baseline noise/spikes) and 187 u (flat-lined above 176 u).

Although 1D telemetry marginally passes thresholds due to high-frequency noise spikes (p125=0.057, p165=0.080 from a noise dip at 166.5 u, diff_125_minus_129=+0.0185) and signal truncation/flat-lining above 180 u (artificially yielding p187=0.068 with apex at 180.5 u), visual inspection of the dual-panel plot confirms the complete absence of true Na+(NaPO3) (125 u), Na+(Na2HPO4) (165 u), and Na+(Na3PO4) (187 u) orthophosphate peaks.

The spectrum fails the 3-P orthophosphate triplet criteria. The anchors are miscalibrated due to early trigger (Na+ 23u at 0.71 us, t0=-1.58 us) with no genuine 63u Na+(NaOH) backbone (only noise above 60u). In the zoomed anion diagnostic window, the trace is pure high-frequency baseline noise without any coherent peaks at 125u (prom=0.110 vs 129u prom=0.149, diff_125_minus_129=-0.0408), 165u, or 187u, and the 81u/63u ratio is 1.01.

The spectrum lacks a distinct salt-rich Na+(NaOH) peak at 63 u (prom=0.094) and exhibits a flat, noisy baseline across 70-195 u without a true orthophosphate triplet. Specifically, 187 u fails the prominence threshold (prom=0.060 < 0.065, apex@181.5 u), the 165 u region is a trough with the local apex shifted left to 158.5 u, and the 125 u region (prom=0.071, apex@122.0 u) consists only of high-frequency baseline noise rather than a resolved Na+(NaPO3) peak.

The spectrum is a textbook carbonate ('3-Car') grain rather than '3-P'. The prominent anion peak in the 120-135 u window is strongly right-shifted into the red 129 u carbonate band (apex at 131.0 u, p125=0.312 vs p129=0.463, diff_125_minus_129=-0.2614), accompanied by a clear 85 u Na+(Na2O) peak. Furthermore, the 165 u orthophosphate band lacks a distinct peak (p165=0.059 with apex at 158.0 u on the decaying tail of the carbonate feature), and the 187 u feature is weak (p187=0.091).

This spectrum is a classic '3-Car' (sodium carbonate) look-alike rather than '3-P'. The prominent anion cluster peak in the 120-135 u region is centered squarely in the red 129 u carbonate band (apex at 129.5 u, prom=0.472 vs 125 u prom=0.433, diff_125_minus_129 = -0.0720), accompanied by a clear 85 u Na+(Na2O) carbonate fragment peak. Furthermore, the diagnostic 165 u and 187 u orthophosphate bands show only a declining tail/noise floor (p165=0.062, p187=0.082 without distinct resolved peaks), failing the orthophosphate triplet criteria.

This spectrum is a classic chloride-dominated ('3-Cl') look-alike rather than a sodium orthophosphate ('3-P') grain. It exhibits a dominant Na+(NaCl) peak at 81 u (prominence = 0.507, 81u/63u ratio = 0.97 > 0.90) and a strong Na+(NaCl)2 peak near 139-143 u (p139 = 0.205 > 0.145), closely matching Reference 9 (SCLK 1477698673). Although there is a peak near 122 u (p125 = 0.195, diff_125_minus_129 = +0.1049), the diagnostic 165 u and 187 u orthophosphate bands are flat (p165 = 0.051, p187 = 0.060 < 0.065).

Visual inspection of the dual-panel plot reveals a classic '3-OH' (sodium hydroxide) spectrum with an elevated flat continuum (~0.70-0.85) and a prominent Na+(NaOH)2 peak near 103 u, rather than a true '3-P' grain. Despite marginally passing automated prominence thresholds due to high-frequency noise on the continuum (p125=0.064, p165=0.061 at 161.5 u, p187=0.085, diff_125_minus_129=+0.0212), the green 165 u band is actually a local minimum/valley (~0.67) and there are no distinct orthophosphate peaks at 125 u, 165 u, or 187 u.

Visual inspection of the dual-panel plot reveals a classic 3-Car (sodium carbonate) morphology rather than a true 3-P orthophosphate triplet. Specifically, because the Na+(NaOH) 63 u peak falls slightly left of the 63 u marker (~60 u due to the lower-bound clamp on the mass-calibration slope a=0.4620 us/sqrt(u)), the single prominent anion peak at calibrated 126.5 u (p125=0.272, diff_125_minus_129=+0.0827) actually corresponds to the shifted 129 u Na+(Na2CO3) carbonate feature. Crucially, the zoomed 70-195 u window shows a monotonically declining tail from 130 u to 195 u with complete absence of true Na+(Na2HPO4) 165 u and Na+(Na3PO4) 187 u peaks (the nominal p165=0.104 at 160.0 u and p187=0.125 at 185.0 u are baseline noise fluctuations on the declining carbonate tail).

This spectrum is a classic chloride-dominated '3-Cl' grain (nearly identical to Reference 9), characterized by a massive Na+(NaCl) peak at 81 u (prom=0.630, 81u/63u ratio=0.93 > 0.90) and a strong Na+(NaCl)2 peak at 139 u (prom=0.185 > 0.145). Although telemetry reports a positive diff_125_minus_129 (+0.1064) due to the falling edge of a 120 u peak (apex@120.0u), there are no genuine orthophosphate peaks in the green 165 u or 187 u bands, which remain flat baseline noise.

Classic 3-Car (sodium carbonate) spectrum rather than 3-P: the dominant anion peak in the 120-135 u region is centered at 128.5 u inside the red 129 u carbonate band (diff_125_minus_129 = -0.0208, 129 u prom = 0.478 vs 125 u prom = 0.473) accompanied by a clear 85 u Na+(Na2O) feature, while the 165 u and 187 u orthophosphate bands lack distinct peaks (showing only a decaying carbonate tail that flatlines above 182.5 u).

The spectrum fails the orthophosphate triplet check and exhibits a classic 3-Car (sodium carbonate) morphology. Specifically, the prominent feature in the 120-135 u window is shifted strongly into the red 129 u carbonate band (apex at 131.0 u, 125 u prom=0.177 vs 129 u prom=0.318, diff_125_minus_129=-0.1430), and the 165 u and 187 u green bands show only a monotonically declining tail rather than distinct Na+(Na2HPO4) and Na+(Na3PO4) peaks.

This spectrum is a classic '3-Cl' (chloride-rich) look-alike closely matching Reference 9 (SCLK 1477698673), disqualified by dominant Na+(NaCl) at 81 u (prom=0.560, 81u/63u ratio=1.03 > 0.90) and Na+(NaCl)2 at 139 u (prom=0.358 > 0.145). Although diff_125_minus_129 is +0.1137 due to a chloride/hydroxide cluster peaking left of the green band at 121.5 u (prom=0.195), the zoomed window shows flat baseline/clipping across the 165 u (prom=0.116 artifact, no peak) and 187 u (prom=0.148 artifact from flat-line clipping at 180 u) orthophosphate bands.

The spectrum fails the orthophosphate triplet criteria and exhibits a classic sodium hydroxide (3-OH) series at 63 u, 103 u, 143 u, and 183 u with a minor carbonate feature centered squarely in the red 129 u band (apex at 129.0 u, p125=0.080 vs p129=0.111, diff_125_minus_129=-0.0398). Furthermore, the green 165 u and 187 u phosphate bands contain only flat baseline noise (p165=0.070 at 161.5 u, p187=0.061 at 180.5 u from the 183 u hydroxide line), ruling out 3-P.

Lacks the characteristic 63 u Na+(NaOH) salt backbone (h=0.51, prom=0.109, 81u/63u ratio=1.03) and fails the orthophosphate triplet check: the 120-135 u region is noisy and shifted toward 129-132 u (p125=0.082 vs p129=0.097, diff_125_minus_129=-0.0151, apex@132.0u), with no genuine peaks at 165 u (p165=0.086 is high-frequency noise) or 187 u (p187=0.111 at 180.0 u, outside the 187 u band).

Visual inspection of the mass-calibrated spectrum reveals a classic sodium hydroxide (3-OH) cluster series dominated by sharp peaks at 23 u (Na+), 41 u (Na(H2O)+), 63 u (Na+(NaOH)), 103 u (Na+(NaOH)2), and 183 u (Na+(NaOH)4). Although the automated telemetry marginally passes the numerical thresholds due to noise at 125 u (prom=0.065) and 165 u (prom=0.061) and the 183 u hydroxide peak bleeding into the 187 u window (apex at 183.5 u, prom=0.091), there are no genuine orthophosphate peaks at 125 u, 165 u, or 187 u.

This spectrum is a pure sodium hydroxide ('3-OH') grain characterized by sharp peaks at 23 u (Na+), 63 u (Na+(NaOH)), and 103 u (Na+(NaOH)2), followed by a flat baseline at higher masses. The orthophosphate triplet at 125 u, 165 u, and 187 u is visually absent (just baseline noise), and the 125 vs 129 u alignment fails (diff_125_minus_129 = -0.0181 with apex at 132.0 u; p125=0.098, p165=0.057, p187=0.078 are merely minor noise fluctuations).

This spectrum is a classic Type 3 Chloride ('3-Cl') look-alike rather than a true '3-P' orthophosphate grain, matching Reference 9 (SCLK 1477698673). It is disqualified by a dominant Na+(NaCl) peak at 81 u (prominence = 0.526, 81u/63u ratio = 0.95 > 0.90) and a strong Na+(NaCl)2 peak at 139 u (prominence = 0.241 > 0.145). Although the mixed chloride-hydroxide cluster near 121-123 u produces a positive diff_125_minus_129 (+0.1208, prom = 0.202), the zoomed diagnostic window shows a flat baseline across both the 165 u (nominal prom = 0.119 from noise, no coherent peak) and 187 u (prom = 0.086, apex shifted to 180.5 u) orthophosphate bands.

The spectrum is dominated by the sodium hydroxide cluster series at 63 u, 103 u, 143 u, and 183 u (3-OH) with a carbonate peak centered at 129.5 u in the red 129 u band (p125=0.089 vs p129=0.144, diff_125_minus_129=-0.0554 < 0). Furthermore, the 165 u region is a flat valley (save for a minor noise spike at 167.5 u with p165=0.078) and the high-mass peak is aligned with 183 u Na+(NaOH)4 (apex at 183.0 u) rather than the 187 u orthophosphate line.

This spectrum is a classic chloride-dominated ('3-Cl') grain, virtually identical to Reference 9 (SCLK 1477698673). It is disqualified from '3-P' by massive Na+(NaCl) at 81 u (p81 = 0.729, 81u/63u ratio = 0.98 > 0.90) and Na+(NaCl)2 at 139 u (p139 = 0.521 > 0.145). Furthermore, the peak near 125 u is actually centered at 121 u (outside the 122-127.5 u green band), and both the 165 u and 187 u orthophosphate green bands are flat/valleys (apices at 161.5 u and 180.5 u despite nominal prom values of 0.085 and 0.129 from flanking features).

This spectrum is a Chloride/Hydroxide-rich look-alike ('3-Cl' / '3-OH') rather than '3-P'. It triggers the Chloride veto with a strong peak at ~82 u (81u/63u ratio = 0.99 > 0.90, prom = 0.189) and a prominent peak at 140-143 u (139u prom = 0.139). Although telemetry reports minor prominences in the 125u (0.087), 165u (0.077), and 187u (0.095) windows with diff_125_minus_129 = +0.0865, visual inspection of the zoomed window reveals no true 165 u peak (only flat baseline noise) and the ~184.5 u feature aligns with the 183 u Na+(NaOH)4 hydroxide line rather than the 187 u Na3PO4 line (which is a valley at 187-190 u).

The spectrum fails the 3-P orthophosphate alignment check and displays classic carbonate-hydroxide (3-Car/3-OH) series peaks. Specifically, the peak in the 120-135 u region is centered squarely in the red 129 u carbonate band (apex at 129.0 u, 125u prom=0.265 vs 129u prom=0.315, diff_125_minus_129 = -0.0711 < 0), accompanied by secondary peaks aligned at 103 u (OH_2), 143 u (OH_3), 169 u (3-Car, apex at 169.5 u rather than 165 u), and 183-185 u (OH_4, apex at 185.5 u rather than 187 u).

Visual inspection of the zoomed anion window (70-195 u) reveals a flat hydroxide-type (3-OH / 3-KNa) continuum rather than a true orthophosphate triplet. Although marginal noise fluctuations barely cross the automated thresholds (125u prom=0.066, 165u prom=0.047@161.0u, 187u prom=0.069@184.0u, diff_125_minus_129=+0.0131), there are no distinct, well-formed peaks at 125 u, 165 u, or 187 u—Instead, the spectrum exhibits a strong K+ (39 u) / Na(H2O)+ (41 u) doublet and Na+(NaOH)n clusters (63 u, 103 u, 143 u, 183 u) characteristic of non-3-P hydroxide/potassium-bearing salt grains.

The spectrum exhibits a strong salt-rich backbone (23 u Na+ and 63 u Na+(NaOH) with prom=0.420) and a well-resolved orthophosphate triplet at 125 u (prom=0.087, apex at 126.5 u), 165 u (prom=0.197, apex at 168.0 u), and 187 u (prom=0.263, apex at 191.5 u). The 125 u peak aligns within the green phosphate band rather than the 129 u carbonate band (diff_125_minus_129 = +0.0311), and chloride features at 81 u (prom=0.057, 81u/63u=0.51) and 139 u (prom=0.024) are negligible, confirming a true '3-P' sodium orthophosphate grain.

The spectrum exhibits a clear salt-rich backbone with dominant Na+ (23 u) and Na+(NaOH) (63 u, prom=0.265) alongside a well-aligned orthophosphate triplet: 125 u Na+(NaPO3) peak (prom=0.052, apex at 126.5 u inside the green band, with diff_125_minus_129 = +0.0175 ruling out 129 u carbonate), a distinct 165 u Na+(Na2HPO4) peak (prom=0.074, apex at 167.0 u), and a strong 187 u Na+(Na3PO4) peak (prom=0.154). Chloride features at 81 u (prom=0.030) and 139 u (prom=-0.001) are negligible.

The peak in the 120-135 u region is strongly shifted into the red 129 u carbonate band (apex at 131.0 u, 125 u prom=0.148 vs 129 u prom=0.225, diff_125_minus_129=-0.0769). Furthermore, visual inspection of the zoomed window shows no coherent orthophosphate peaks at 165 u or 187 u (apparent telemetry prominences of 0.155 and 0.157 are artifacts of deep downward baseline noise spikes around 175-177 u). This is a carbonate-bearing (3-Car) spectrum rather than 3-P.

The spectrum fails the orthophosphate triplet criteria and is dominated by sodium hydroxide clusters (strong peaks at 63 u, 103 u, and 143 u) alongside a carbonate feature. Specifically, the peak in the 120-135 u region is centered at 129.5 u inside the red 129 u carbonate band rather than at 125 u (125 u prom=0.127 vs 129 u prom=0.149, diff_125_minus_129=-0.0311), and visual inspection of the zoomed window confirms flat baseline noise across both the 165 u (apex shifted to 161.5 u) and 187 u (apex shifted to 183.5 u) green phosphate bands.

This spectrum is a classic chloride-dominated ('3-Cl') look-alike rather than a true '3-P' grain. It fails the chloride veto with a dominant Na+(NaCl) peak at 81 u (prom=0.481 > 0.30, 81u/63u ratio=0.99 > 0.90) and a strong Na+(NaCl)2 feature near 139 u (prom=0.273 > 0.145). Visually, the 125 u, 165 u, and 187 u phosphate regions contain only high-frequency baseline noise and deep dropouts (which artificially inflate the numerical prominence values at 125 u=0.186, 165 u=0.181, and 187 u=0.147 despite diff_125_minus_129=+0.0398), with no coherent orthophosphate triplet peaks present.

The spectrum lacks the diagnostic 125, 165, and 187 u orthophosphate triplet. In the 120-135 u region, there is no distinct 125 u peak (p125=0.057, diff_125_minus_129=-0.0012, apex@120.0u), and the zoomed window shows flat continuum noise across the 125, 165 (p165=0.061), and 187 u (p187=0.071, apex@182.0u corresponding to the 183 u hydroxide line) bands, along with a clear 103 u Na+(NaOH)2 peak typical of a 3-OH/3-KNa salt grain.

This spectrum is a noisy water-ice/chloride look-alike rather than a true 3-P grain. The anchors are anomalous (t0=-1.52 us, with 19u H3O+ misidentified near 23u and hydronium clusters at 37u=0.21, 55u=0.21, and 81u/63u ratio=0.99 > 0.90). In the zoomed 70-195 u window, the high-mass baseline is purely flat noise with sharp negative dropouts rather than distinct orthophosphate triplet peaks at 125 u, 165 u, and 187 u (apparent prominences p125=0.127, p165=0.196, p187=0.163 are artifacts of deep noise spikes near 151u and 163u, and the 118-135u apex sits at 118.5u outside the 125u band).

Visual inspection of the full-range and zoomed panels shows that this is a potassium-bearing salt grain (3-KNa) dominated by K+ at 39 u (h=1.00 > Na+ 23 u h=0.92) and a 95 u KNa cluster peak, rather than a 3-P sodium orthophosphate grain. Although telemetry reports nominal prominences p125=0.073 (diff_125_minus_129=+0.0394, apex@122.0u), p165=0.066 (apex@161.0u), and p187=0.076 (apex@192.0u), the zoomed 70-195 u plot reveals that the 165 u and 187 u green bands contain only flat baseline noise (~0.23 scaled log amplitude) with apparent prominence driven by single-bin downward noise spikes, lacking true Na+(Na2HPO4) and Na+(Na3PO4) peaks.

Spectrum is a chloride-rich (3-Cl) grain, closely matching Reference 9. It is dominated by a massive 81 u peak (p81=0.541 > 0.30), along with peaks at 103 u, 121.5 u (outside the 122-127.5 u 3-P window), and ~140 u (p139=0.133), while the 165 u and 187 u orthophosphate bands are completely flat and devoid of true peaks.

The spectrum fails the 3-P orthophosphate check and lacks a true salt-rich Type 3 backbone (weak 63 u feature with prom=0.115 and strong low-mass peaks around 15 u and 35 u). Visual inspection of the 70-195 u zoomed window confirms that the apparent prominences at 125 u (0.153, apex at 121.5 u outside the 122-127.5 u band), 165 u (0.259, apex at 160.0 u), 187 u (0.227), and 139 u (0.181) are artifacts of severe high-frequency noise and deep negative baseline dropouts rather than genuine Na+(NaPO3), Na+(Na2HPO4), and Na+(Na3PO4) cluster peaks.

Clear sodium orthophosphate ('3-P') spectrum exhibiting the salt-rich Na+ (23 u) and Na+(NaOH) (63 u) backbone alongside a well-aligned orthophosphate triplet: 125 u Na+(NaPO3) (prom=0.114, apex at 127.0 u inside the green 125 u band with diff_125_minus_129=+0.0534 over 129 u carbonate), 165 u Na+(Na2HPO4) (prom=0.107, apex at 166.0 u), and 187 u Na+(Na3PO4) (prom=0.101, apex at 189.0 u). Chloride features at 81 u (prom=0.047, 81u/63u ratio=0.63) and 139 u (prom=0.052) are low, ruling out 3-Cl.

Fails the 3-P orthophosphate triplet check: the 120-135 u region lacks a distinct 125 u peak and instead peaks in the 129 u band (prom_125=0.057 vs prom_129=0.083, diff_125_minus_129=-0.0259, apex at 128.5 u). Visually, the high-mass anion window (70-195 u) is noisy and monotonically declining with no true peaks at 125 u, 165 u (apex at 159.5 u outside the green band), or 187 u (apex at 181.5 u). Furthermore, the strong K+ peak at 39 u, weak 63 u Na+(NaOH) backbone, and elevated 81u/63u ratio (0.98) confirm a non-3-P (likely KNa/salt or water-rich) grain.

This spectrum is a classic carbonate ('3-Car') look-alike rather than a true '3-P' grain. In the 120-135 u region, the prominent peak is centered squarely in the red 129 u carbonate band (apex at 129.5 u, prom=0.381 vs 125 u prom=0.334, yielding diff_125_minus_129 = -0.0497 < 0). Furthermore, the zoomed diagnostic window shows a descending tail/flat baseline across the green 165 u (actual local apex at 159.5 u) and 187 u (flat clipped tail above 181 u) orthophosphate bands, confirming the absence of the Na+(Na2HPO4) and Na+(Na3PO4) peaks.

The spectrum is a classic hydroxide/carbonate-rich grain (strong 63 u, 103 u, and 143 u Na+(NaOH)n series with a 129-130 u carbonate feature) rather than a 3-P orthophosphate grain. In the 120-135 u region, the peak apex sits at 130.0 u in the red 129 u carbonate band (p125=0.108 vs p129=0.139, diff_125_minus_129=-0.0387). Furthermore, the green 165 u band is a flat baseline valley (nominal p165=0.054 is noise at 171 u) and the 187 u region drops off right after the 183 u Na+(NaOH)4 feature (apex at 182.5 u).

Clear textbook '3-P' sodium orthophosphate spectrum. It exhibits a strong salt-rich backbone with Na+ (23u, h=1.00) and Na+(NaOH) (63u, h=0.85, prom=0.392) alongside all three prominent orthophosphate triplet peaks: 125u Na+(NaPO3) (prom=0.212, apex@126.5u, aligned with the 125u band rather than the 129u carbonate band with diff_125_minus_129=+0.0159), 165u Na+(Na2HPO4) (prom=0.209), and 187u Na+(Na3PO4) (prom=0.284). Chloride features at 81u (prom=-0.002) and 139u (prom=0.002) are absent.

This spectrum is a classic chloride-dominated ('3-Cl') look-alike rather than a true '3-P' grain. It fails the chloride veto with a dominant Na+(NaCl) peak at 81 u (p81 = 0.344 > 0.30, 81u/63u ratio = 1.07 > 0.90) and a strong Na+(NaCl)2 feature near 139-143 u (p139 = 0.199 > 0.145). Furthermore, visual inspection confirms the absence of a true orthophosphate triplet: the 165 u and 187 u green bands contain only low-level baseline noise (with the nominal 165 u window apex shifted to 159.0 u) despite a minor bump near 123 u (p125 = 0.201, diff_125_minus_129 = +0.0132).

The spectrum is a classic carbonate ('3-Car') grain rather than '3-P'. The major peak in the 120-140 u region is strongly shifted into the red 129 u carbonate band (prom=0.351 at 129 u vs prom=0.228 at 125 u, diff_125_minus_129=-0.1268, apex at 133.5 u). Furthermore, the diagnostic 165 u Na+(Na2HPO4) and 187 u Na+(Na3PO4) peaks are absent in the zoomed plot, which shows only a decaying baseline across the 165 u and 187 u green bands.

This spectrum is a classic chloride-dominated ('3-Cl') look-alike rather than a true '3-P' grain. It fails the chloride veto with a dominant Na+(NaCl) peak at 81 u (prominence 0.437, 81u/63u ratio = 1.03 > 0.90) and a strong Na+(NaCl)2 peak near 139-143 u (prominence 0.174 > 0.145). Visually, the 165 u and 187 u orthophosphate bands contain only baseline noise and flatline clipping rather than genuine Na+(Na2HPO4) and Na+(Na3PO4) peaks, despite the minor feature at 123.5 u (p125=0.178, diff_125_minus_129=+0.0432).

The target spectrum exhibits a textbook orthophosphate triplet signature: (1) a well-resolved Na+(NaPO3) peak centered directly on the green 125 u line (apex at 125.0 u, p125=0.238 >= 0.050) rather than the red 129 u carbonate band (diff_125_minus_129=+0.0691), (2) a distinct Na+(Na2HPO4) peak in the 165 u green band (apex at 164.0 u, p165=0.223 >= 0.045), and (3) a strong Na+(Na3PO4) peak in the 187 u green band (apex at 188.5 u, p187=0.287 >= 0.065), with no chloride dominance (81u/63u ratio=0.40, p81=0.086).

Classic 3-Car (sodium carbonate) spectrum. The dominant high-mass peak in the 120-135 u region sits squarely in the red 129 u carbonate band (apex at 129.0 u, prom=0.607 vs 125 u prom=0.565, diff_125_minus_129=-0.0735), accompanied by a distinct 85 u Na+(Na2O) peak. Furthermore, the 165 u and 187 u orthophosphate bands show no true peaks (only a declining carbonate tail and low-level noise), ruling out 3-P.

Visual inspection of the mass-calibrated spectrum reveals a classic Type 3 sodium hydroxide ('3-OH') cluster series with distinct peaks at 23 u, 63 u, 103 u, 143 u, and 183 u (Na+(NaOH)_n for n=0..4), rather than an orthophosphate triplet. Although the automated 1D telemetry marginally passes threshold checks (p125=0.057, p165=0.051, p187=0.066, diff_125_minus_129=+0.0009), the 187 u prominence actually measures the adjacent 183 u Na+(NaOH)4 peak (apex at 181.5 u) while the 187 u band slopes downward, the 165 u region is a deep flat valley between the 143 u and 183 u hydroxide peaks, and the 125-129 u region lacks a true Na+(NaPO3) peak.

Visual inspection of the dual-panel plot reveals a flat, declining hydroxide-like (3-OH) continuum from 70 to 200 u without genuine orthophosphate peaks at 125 u, 165 u, or 187 u. Although telemetry reports positive prominences at 125 u (0.078), 165 u (0.154, apex@159.5u), and 187 u (0.153, apex@182.0u) with diff_125_minus_129=+0.0081, the zoomed panel shows that these prominence values are artifacts of isolated negative noise dropouts at ~156 u and ~178 u rather than true emission peaks in the green 125, 165, and 187 u bands.

Visual inspection of the dual-panel mass-calibrated spectrum reveals a classic sodium hydroxide ('3-OH') signature dominated by Na+ (23 u), Na+(NaOH) (63 u), and a sharp Na+(NaOH)2 dimer peak at 103 u, with no true orthophosphate triplet features above the baseline noise. Although 1D telemetry reports marginal noise-level prominences at 125 u (0.070), 165 u (0.083, apex shifted to 161.5 u), and 187 u (0.084, apex at 183.5 u OH_4 line), the green diagnostic bands at 125 u, 165 u, and 187 u contain only flat baseline fluctuations rather than coherent Na+(NaPO3), Na+(Na2HPO4), and Na+(Na3PO4) peaks.
